 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 30.10.2021 passed by the Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT-II, Yadgir, in MVC No.65 of 2020.
2.
The claimant, aged 18 years, student met with an accident on 14.06.2019 and sustained grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.11,00,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.4,32,413/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.1-Corporation to deposit the same.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6864 HC-KAR 3.
Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that the Tribunal has granted inadequate compensation.
The Doctor assessed the disability at 17%, but the Tribunal has taken only 10%.
He was earning Rs,12,000/- per month by doing milk vending business, but the Tribunal has not considered his income.
The interest awarded at 6% p.a. and it is to be enhanced to 9% p.a., therefore requested for enhancement of compensation.

2 4. Heard the arguments of both sides.
5. The age of the appellant was 16 years at the time of accident.

sentences.text: He sustained fracture of right tibia and implant was fixed.
PW.2 assessed the disability as 17%.

Therefore, the Tribunal has relied upon the citation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in AIR 2014 SC 736 and as the disability is more than 10%, awarded NC: 2025:KHC-K:6864 HC-KAR an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-
towards loss of future earnings.

entities.text: Master Mallikarjun vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Another reported in AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apart from that, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.92,413/- towards medical expenses and also Rs.25,000/- for removal of implants, which are just and proper and needs no interference.

6. Further, considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.25,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.15,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.

7. Hence, the total compensation would be as under:
Pain and suffering Rs.25,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.92,413/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges

Loss of future earnings Rs.3,00,000/-
Loss of amenities Rs.15,000/-
Removal of implants Rs.25,000/-
Total Rs.4,87,413/-
 NC: 2025:KHC-K:6864 HC-KAR

Thus, the appellant is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,87,413/- as against Rs.4,32,413/-
awarded by the Tribunal, with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.
8. In the result, the following order is passed:
( i) Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for Sabareddy S/O Bhimappa Bagali vs The Divisional Controller And Anr on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102654745/
3 total compensation of Rs.4,87,413/- as against Rs.4,32,413/- awarded by the Tribunal, with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

Respondent No.1-Corpraiton is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6864 HC-KAR (iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
